newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen down on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen down on Wednesday.

text.p: Polish shares on Tuesday fell for the second straight session and analysts said dominant selling after price fixing signalled another fall on Wednesday as investors were reluctant to buy amid a lack of positive signs.
"We seem to have stagnation now, with the market waiting for another impulse," said Jan Koch, a trader at Polish Development Bank (PBR) brokerage.

Analysts said an impulse could come on Wednesday when the Senate may vote on 1997's tax rates. Last month parliament's lower house voted to cut taxes for lower earners, a move seen as inflationary that helped cause market falls.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 1.1 percent to 13,716.3 points and turnover fell eight percent to 68.6 million zlotys ($24.5 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 39 to 23 with 18 stocks stable.
Analysts put strong support at 13,200 points.
They said firms' October earnings data next week should affect the market more than the month's inflation figure due this Friday, as the central bank has pledged no quick rate cut.

Analysts were surprised by loss leader construction firm Remak's 6.5-percent fall after having dropped 10 percent last week. They said brewer Zywiec and and industrial and trading conglomerate Elektrim fell four and 3.5 percent in profit-taking after big gains last week.
Continuous trade turnover was at 1.1 million zlotys ($0.4 milion) with biggest mover Rolimpex down 3.6 percent.

Mass privatisation NFI units fell 1.8 percent to 138 zlotys ($49.3) in the regular bourse session and fell 0.7 percent to 135.5 zlotys ($48.5) in continuous trade. Some analysts said NFI falls could continue as the November 22 deadline appoaches for Poles to buy their unit on the primary market.
